title: Holman Erection v. Orville E. Madsen & Sons
shortTitle: Holman Erection v. Orville E. Madsen & Sons
summary: Using and listing a subcontractor’s bid did not necessarily accept it or create reciprocal estoppel.
notes:
Casebook discussion of a shorter authority.

The general contractor won but selected another firm. The reported decision affirmed summary judgment against the subcontractor. The explanation points to ordinary bidding costs, bids to multiple generals, and selection factors beyond price. The case tests the claimed symmetry of Drennan without denying that an actual promise or additional conduct could change the analysis.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 258–259. Open assigned page 258.
